newsitem.title: USA: Some U.S. computer makers Q1 seen hurt by currency.
newsitem.headline: Some U.S. computer makers Q1 seen hurt by currency.

text.p: Most U.S. computer hardware makers will begin reporting first quarter earnings this week, with the stronger dollar expected to erode the revenue growth rate at companies with big overseas operations, analysts said.
The first quarter is also typically a more sluggish quarter, after the big fourth quarter, especially in PCs, where a new multimedia chip did not provide much of a boost.
Analysts said that product transitions also played a part in some large systems vendors earnings, as customers held off buying as they wait for new products due later this year.

"What seemed like a currency-neutral year is turning negative," said John Jones, a Salomon Brothers analyst. "It's a big factor for all the multi-nationals doing business in local currencies - IBM (and) Digital."

Companies like International Business Machines Corp and Digital Equipment Corp, both of which derive a large portion of revenues from outside the U.S., will see their earnings hurt the most from a stronger dollar.
When the exchange rate of the dollar versus foreign currency climbs, revenues earned in those foreign currencies are worth less when they are translated back to U.S currency.
IBM is expected to have a fairly large earnings hit from currency this quarter, of at least $0.20 a share, analysts estimate.
They said another potential negative factor stems from customers' anticipation of a new IBM mainframe upgrade.

This has led customers to hold off on such purchases until the new product is out, which is expected in June. But the strength in its services, storage and UNIX-based workstation growth will offset the continued decline in mainframes.

Digital Equipment is also expected to have a negative currency impact and analysts expect it to report sluggish Alpha-based workstation revenues, which may offset some expected growth in Alpha-based servers.

Unisys Corp is expected to report a loss, and analysts said they are hoping its new mainframe rollout will help its earnings recover later this year. Amdahl Corp, another mainframe computer developer, is expected to either post a slight loss or break-even earnings, as softness continues in the large system part of its business.
In the PC sector, analysts said companies did not see too much of a hoped-for boost from the arrival of mulitimedia technology in the form of a new Intel Corp chip.
"The March quarter appears to be demonstrating the typical seasonal pattern," said John Dean, a Salomon Brothers analyst.
The leaders in the PC industry, Compaq Computer Corp and direct sellers Dell Computer Corp and Gateway 2000 Inc, should post solid, in-line numbers.
Apple Computer Inc will report, as previously announced, a hefty loss. But analysts said they were optimistic about new products boosting the rest of the year.

"The key for Apple is the next two quarters, to see if they can actually turn the ship around," said Louis Mazzicchelli, an analyst with Gerard Klauer Mattison. "The signs are good...the product line is the best it's been in a long time."
